visuals.title: Which EQUIP focus is LIP oversight?
visuals.prompt: Select the EQUIP focus area that covers lead interpreting physician review of QA/QC test frequency and corrective-action appropriateness.

feedback.a: That box is the poor-image corrective-action / IP feedback focus.
feedback.b: That box is the periodic sample clinical image review focus.
feedback.c: Correct. LIP oversight is the third EQUIP focus: QA/QC frequency and corrective-action review.

visuals.explanation: EQUIP's three inspection foci are corrective action with IP feedback, periodic sample clinical image review, and LIP oversight of QA/QC records including test frequency and corrective-action appropriateness.

visuals.title: Where do unresolved serious complaints go?
visuals.prompt: A serious complaint cannot be resolved at the facility. Select the next regulatory destination the consumer must be directed toward.

feedback.a: The facility tries first, but the question asks where unresolved serious complaints are directed.
feedback.b: This step is the instruction to file with the accreditation body—the destination itself is the accreditation body.
feedback.c: Correct. Unresolved serious complaints are filed with the facility's accreditation body, and the facility reports them there.

visuals.explanation: § 900.12(h) requires the facility to give directions for filing unresolved serious complaints with its accreditation body and to report those unresolved complaints to the body.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Steps are named; selecting any step is keyboard accessible.

visuals.title: Which retention rule applies?
visuals.prompt: A patient had only one mammogram at your facility and never returned. State law requires 7 years. Select the federal box that forces a longer retention than the 5-year floor.

hotspots.revealLabel: 10-year rule applies when no later mammo at facility
State 7 years is shorter than 10 here

feedback.a: Five years is the federal floor, but with no later mammogram the 10-year rule applies.
feedback.b: Correct. No additional mammograms at the facility triggers the at-least-10-years rule, which is longer than both 5 and this State's 7.
feedback.c: State law matters when it is longer; here 7 years is shorter than the federal 10-year no-return rule.

visuals.explanation: Retention uses the longest of 5 years, 10 years if no later mammograms at the facility, or a longer State/local mandate.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Boxes are labeled by duration rule.

visuals.title: Which timing bucket for a failed phantom test?
visuals.prompt: A required phantom image QC test is outside action limits. Select the corrective-action timing bucket that applies before patients may be imaged on the failed component.

feedback.a: Correct. Phantom image testing is on the before-further-examinations list in § 900.12(e)(8).
feedback.b: Thirty days applies to other equipment QA tests that are not on the before-further-exams list.

visuals.explanation: § 900.12(e)(8) splits failures into before-further-exams (including phantom, compression device, dose, and digital manufacturer QC) versus within 30 days for other listed equipment tests.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Buckets are named by timing rule.

glossary.definition: Enhancing Quality Using the Inspection Program: FDA's addition of annual inspection questions on clinical image corrective action, periodic sample image review, and lead interpreting physician oversight of QA/QC.
Documented review, at least annually since the last inspection, of image-quality attributes on a sample of mammograms from each active technologist and each active interpreting physician.
Minimum and maximum acceptable values for a quality assurance measurement; results outside them require identifying the problem and correcting it on the required timeline.
A report of a serious adverse event (for example poor image quality, late required reports, or unqualified personnel).
Anyone who comments or complains about a mammography examination, including the patient or a representative such as a family member or referring physician.

For FFDM/DBT and other non-screen-film receptors, MQSA requires a QA program substantially the same as the image-receptor manufacturer's recommendations, while still obeying the federal phantom dose ceiling.
Physicist assessment after installation, reassembly, or major repair/change; problems must be corrected before clinical use.
FDA-directed review of clinical images and related information when quality may present a serious risk to human health, which can lead to required patient or public notification.
An FDA-accepted alternative standard some facilities use for digital mammography QC procedures; Mammo links to it and does not redistribute its worksheets or pass/fail tables.
